title: Shared Gaussian input errors raised total-area SD by 52-594 times in a reference model for six USGS landslide maps
abstract: We test whether cell uncertainty in six archived USGS landslide maps can set uncertainty in total landslide area. We reuse a published Gaussian input-error reference and fixed selected cells. We keep each cell distribution unchanged and vary only dependence. A common Gaussian error gives the exact largest total variance over all joint laws with these marginals. Its total-area standard deviation (SD) is 52-594 times the independent-cell SD. A smooth Gaussian field with latent pair correlation 0.01 raises SD by 4.0-53.3 times. At twice each reference mean, the common-error exceedance probability is 12.3-14.5%. The independent-cell probability is at most 0.00025-0.1024%, by Cantelli's inequality. We give a scalable Hermite method for a shared Gaussian factor and an upper risk bound that allows any dependence. The latter is 34.3-44.3% at this threshold. The proof and methods use known probability results; the contribution is their application and reproducible tools for these maps. This is a conditional model study, not observed landslide calibration. Six selected later products, an assumed Gaussian error law and fixed masks limit the scope. The results show that a cellwise uncertainty repair alone does not set regional area risk.

display.caption: The same conditional cell distributions give very different regional uncertainty. The common Gaussian field attains maximum variance; it does not maximise every tail probability.

citations.reason: Reuses the six-case selection and Gaussian marginal reference, and resolves part of its open regional dependence problem.
Known comonotonic convex-order bound; no claim of a new theorem.
